headline: High: Mentat’s broad network egress plus filesystem writes can leak or corrupt content if paired with a content source that is treated as trusted.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no shared channel or I/O surface beyond being a content-writing source, while B reads/writes files and can ingest file content as input. The pair lacks a documented direct bridge, so prompt injection is possible mainly through manual file handoff or copied content, which is a limited pathway.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into files that agent_b reads as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace is introduced outside the profiles, the attack surface increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Review any A-generated text before placing it into B inputs.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files by B.
Use a manual approval step for any prompt-like content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for A outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B reads selected files and has broad network egress, so file contents can leave the local environment through its model-provider calls. A is a content-writing source with broad network egress but no filesystem surface; the pair can therefore move sensitive file content from B into externally hosted inference, even though A itself does not expose files.
conditions: IF selected files contain secrets or regulated data, B can transmit them to its provider.
IF A-generated content is combined with B-read files, the combined context may also leave the environment.
mitigations: Restrict B to non-sensitive files.
Use a local-only model provider for B.
Redact secrets before passing files to B.
Separate A-generated drafts from B-managed source trees.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B can write files and modify git state, and its shared state is explicitly via filesystem. A has broad network egress but no write surface, so direct write-write conflict is not shown; however, if A’s outputs are materialized into the same tree, B can overwrite or commit them without coordination. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A outputs are saved into the same repository or directory B edits, file conflicts can occur.
IF multiple B instances run concurrently, filesystem-based shared state can race.
mitigations: Run only one B instance per workspace.
Use separate directories for A and B artifacts.
Commit or snapshot before B edits.
Avoid concurrent git operations in the same repo.
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B produces diff-based edit proposals and applies edits after user confirmation, so it can treat A’s content as an input source for code or text changes. A is a content-writing agent, making it plausible that B will render or act on A’s output without strong verification. The confirmation step reduces but does not eliminate the cascade.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as authoritative source material, downstream edits can propagate errors.
IF the user approves B’s proposed diff without checking A’s claims, the cascade completes.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Ask B to cite source files for every factual claim.
Limit B to mechanical edits only.
Compare B proposals against original inputs.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before diff application.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. B handles model-provider API keys and source code, while A exposes only a content-writing category and broad egress; the evidence does not show a concrete compliance breach, so this remains a low, documentation-gap risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s selected files, compliance obligations may change.
IF deployment policy requires specific residency or retention controls, the current profiles do not document them.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in B inputs.
Confirm provider residency and retention settings.
Document data-handling responsibilities for both agents.
Store API keys outside shared workspaces.
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement.
